Question: Tom’s Hat Shoppe increased all original prices by \(25\%.\) Now the shoppe is having a sale where all prices are \(20\%\) off these increased prices. Which statement best describes the sale price of an item?

Choices.A: The sale price is \(5\%\) higher than the original price.
Choices.B:
The sale price is higher than the original price, but by less
than \(5\%.\)
Choices.C:
The sale price is higher than the original price, but by more
than \(5\%.\)
Choices.D: The sale price is lower than the original price.
Choices.E:
The sale price is the same as the original
price.

Solution:
The discount applies to the increased price, so we must apply the two changes in succession. Let the original price be \(P>0\) dollars. Increasing it by \(25\%\) makes it \(125\%=\frac54\) of its original value. Taking \(20\%\) off then leaves \(80\%=\frac45\) of that increased price. Thus the sale price is
\[
\frac45\left(\frac54P\right)=P.
\]
The sale price is the same as the original price, choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
